raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both papers are companion articles reporting empirical findings from the exact same 2000-2001 PhD dissertation fieldwork by Laila Smith (at Clark University, where Study B co-author Susan Hanson was based) examining commercialization/corporatization and cost-recovery water policies over 1997-2001 in the Cape Town and Tygerberg administrations of the Cape Metropolitan Area, South Africa. Both studies draw on the same stratified household interview sample of N = 120 households across the same four Coloured and African townships (Langa, Mitchells Plain, Khayelitsha, and Bonteheuwell, stratified by standpipes, yard taps, and in-house connections), the same municipal official interviews/fieldwork, and the exact same 1999-2001 municipal water disconnection records (159,886 total cutoffs: 16,964 in Cape Town and 142,922 in Tygerberg, including 77,000 in 2001, 14,355 in Khayelitsha over six months, 902 per 1,000 billed customers in Mumfuleni, and a 60% illegal reconnection rate in Tygerberg). Study A explicitly cites Study B (Smith and Hanson, 2003) and directly reprints Figures 5 and 6 of Study B as Figures 4 and 5 of Study A, while framing three cost-recovery policies (pricing/tariffs, outsourcing, and debt management/cutoffs) alongside ~100 institutional interviews; Study B provides fuller tabular and regression/discriminant analyses of the N = 120 household survey focusing on infrastructure underinvestment and debt management/cutoffs.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Case study of water sector commercialization/corporatization (1997-2001) in the Cape Town and Tygerberg administrations, Cape Metropolitan Area, South Africa, based on 9 months of PhD dissertation fieldwork in 2000-2001 comprising interviews with ~100 local authority officials, politicians, union shop stewards, and civil society representatives; N = 120 stratified household interviews across four Coloured and African townships (including Langa, Khayelitsha, and Mitchells Plain); municipal water tariff schedules (1997-2002); and municipal billing/disconnection data (N = 159,886 household water cutoffs in 1999-2001: 16,964 in Cape Town and 142,922 in Tygerberg).
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Case study of water commercialization and cost recovery (1997-2001) in the Cape Town and Tygerberg administrations, Cape Metropolitan Area, South Africa, based on 2000-2001 fieldwork by the first author: N = 120 semi-structured household interviews conducted in 2001 across four Coloured and African townships (Langa and Mitchells Plain in Cape Town; Khayelitsha and Bonteheuwell in Tygerberg; 30 per township across standpipe, yard tap, and in-house neighbourhoods, including N = 90 billed and N = 57 in-arrears subsamples), a 2000 metro-wide water depot audit, official interviews/communications, and municipal water disconnection/reconnection data (N = 159,886 water cutoffs in 1999-2001: 16,964 in Cape Town and 142,922 in Tygerberg).
